parsedVerdict.reasoning: This unit is a single file with one class, SessionDocumentRepository, which implements the SessionRepository port on top of Mongoose. Every method deals with storing sessions (find, create, update, update by hash, and the three delete methods), so the file covers one concern. The module's own abstractions are used consistently: all conversions between documents and the domain go through SessionMapper.toDomain/toPersistence, and all queries go through the injected Model<SessionSchemaClass>. Two small points do not amount to a violation. First, the list of fields that cannot be changed (id, createdAt, updatedAt, deletedAt) appears twice: once as the delete statements in update() and once in the Omit type in updateByHash(). Both are in the same file and follow the shape of the port contract, so this is not a rule copied across files. Second, updateByHash() writes { hash: payload.hash } directly to the model instead of passing it through the mapper. That only changes the value of a field the schema and the domain share, so it does not get around the mapping layer for domain-to-document conversion. The result is still mapped back through SessionMapper.toDomain.
